claim.why_it_matters: Three places merge separate index entries into one line. One of them joins a sub-entry (File description entry, under BLOCK CONTAINS clause) to two top-level headwords, so the entry boundaries and the parent/child structure are lost.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of printed page 839 (PDF page 861) shows each of these as a separate index line: 'WRITE statement 558' (indented sub-entry continuing from the previous page) then 'ATAN function 579' at top level; 'B PICTURE symbol 313', 'BACKGROUND-COLOR clause 262', 'B-AND operator 118' as three top-level lines; and at the top of the right column the indented sub-entry 'File description entry 234' (child of 'BLOCK CONTAINS clause 268', which ends the left column) followed by top-level 'Boolean category 111, 112, 292, 316' and 'Boolean character 8'. The markdown runs each group together on one line with no break or \ separator, and gives the merged lines a leading indent, so 'ATAN function', 'Boolean category' and 'Boolean character' look like sub-entries and the entry boundaries are lost. No words or page numbers are missing; the defect is lost entry and hierarchy structure. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The page is an informative index, so the defect does not affect normative content.
